en: But now my daughter, too, has been struck
by an illness like this...

note: Six dots shown as '...'. Shared: Epstein, and the player's silent reply to Vivian and Nellie.

en: If I lose my daughter as well as my wife,
what on earth am I to do?
What I want most of all now
is for my only daughter, Rose, to be happy.
Wh-what are you doing
note: Followed by #265 x3 with pauses and #122: 'Wh-what are you doing...!' (cut off as he is attacked).

en: ...Count.
I must borrow your strength for a while.
I'm terribly sorry, but
no one may enter without an introduction.
Some sort of password was needed, as I recall.
White Lily
note: Answer choice (no used_in). Password is 'Black Rose' as in slice 003/004.

en: Black Rose
note: Answer choice; the correct password ("Black Rose" in slices 003/004).

en: Red Poppy

note: No final period: Pauline uses it before the name: '...Chris?'.

en: Please, come in.
This is a gambling den.
It is not, of course, a licensed one,
so we ask for your discretion.
Now then, do enjoy yourself.
Please leave.
Take your time.
note: No used_in; Philip's line, meaning inferred.

en: Winning at gambling is not everything
in life, you know.
And yet so many people want to stake
everything on a wager.
A pistol in the right hand, banknotes in the left...
Some wagers are a deadly roulette.
If one can use a pistol and banknotes well,
perhaps one has no real need to gamble
in a place like this.
Please, enjoy yourself.
I'll have your blood...
...What are you?
How did you get in here?
I am a vampire.
One who comes and goes like a phantom...
Oho.
How interesting.
To be bitten by a vampire is a novel diversion.
Do as you like with my blood.
...An odd man.
Then I shall do as I like.
I needed some sort of password, didn't I?
Do give this old codger your orders, too.
note: After '{NAME}, my master...' (#754 + #152); starts a new sentence.

en: Who might you be?
My memory's been terrible lately.
Well, hello there.
Now, who might you be?
Ah, yes, of course, of course.
Cold again today.
Now, if only the sun would come out a bit,
it'd be better for painting.
Since olden days, against the sun's whims
we humans have never stood a chance.
Dear me, it's turned quite cold.
It's hard on old bones.
Dear me. My easel and paints have started
to feel heavy.
I'm getting on in years, all right.
Sorry, but I'm tired just now.
Go talk with one of the young folk
in this building.
Sorry, but at home, let me sleep.
Sorry, but at home I'd like to rest easy,
you see.
Leave me be.
Please, leave me be.
Oh, it's you.
Well, come in.
I was just putting color on a painting.
There's nothing here but my painting things.
What are you doing here?
I'm a landscape painter, you see.
I paint here by the river like this.
I've only just begun, so the canvas is blank.
Cold every day, isn't it.
